mechanism: row-to-core balance / evenly spaced sparse-tail owners
hypothesis: Distributing one-row tasks from a sparse final stripe across evenly spaced logical block IDs may spread active block dispatch positions compared with assigning the same tasks to a contiguous block suffix.
change: Only for a non-empty sparse tail after at least one full stripe when rowGroupWidth > 1, use owner positions owner(i) = floor(((i + 1) * blockCount - 1) / tailRows). Each active owner receives one tail row in increasing owner order; inactive owners use tailRows as the zero-row sentinel. All other cases retain prior ownership behavior.

distinction_check.evidence: For blockCount=8 and tailRows=3, R046 active owners are [2,5,7], while R043's suffix owners are [5,6,7]. The active-owner sets differed from the suffix policy in 7,875 of 8,128 enumerated blockCount/tailRows pairs. This changes which logical blocks own the tail, not just traversal order.
distinction_check.scope_note: Hypothesis concerns active logical-block dispersion only; no device core topology or performance benefit is asserted.

commands: inline python3 -c inverse/owner-spacing enumeration for blockCount 2..128 and tailRows 1..blockCount-1
inline python3 -c exact row partition and per-block balance enumeration for blockCount 1..24, groupWidth 1..6, fullGroups 0..4, and every tail length
invariants: Each sparse-tail row maps to exactly one active logical block.
Sparse-tail owner positions are unique and gaps differ by at most one block ID.
Every row across full stripes and tail is assigned exactly once.
Per-block total row counts differ by at most one.
